title: Salman Khan and Nayanthara Are About to Shut Down Bandra. The Action Starts June 10.
excerpt: Their first film together — an untitled action thriller directed by Vamshi Paidipally — moves to Mumbai for chases, combat, and crowd-heavy sequences across one of the city's most iconic neighbourhoods.
body:
If you are anywhere near **Bandra** next week, expect road closures, crowd barriers, and the unmistakable energy of a **Salman Khan** shoot in full swing.

Starting **June 10**, Salman and **Nayanthara** will begin filming a series of high-octane action sequences across multiple outdoor locations in and around Bandra for their yet-untitled film directed by **Vamshi Paidipally**. The schedule, first reported by *Mid-Day*, marks one of the most physically ambitious legs of a production that has already shot in Mumbai studios and **Manali**.

And the sequences sound like they mean business.

> "The team will shoot across multiple outdoor locations in and around Bandra because the sequences require the texture and scale of an urban setting. The sequences, featuring both leads, include chases, vehicle-based action, close-quarter combat, and crowd-heavy moments." — Production source to Mid-Day

## Why This Pairing Matters

This is the **first time Salman Khan and Nayanthara have shared the screen** in a full-fledged lead pairing, and the combination is almost too obvious in retrospect. Salman is the last standing mass hero of Hindi cinema's old guard — the man who still fills single screens from Patna to Peshawar. Nayanthara, the **Lady Superstar** of South Indian cinema, proved she could dominate a Hindi film when she stood opposite Shah Rukh Khan in *Jawan* and refused to be overshadowed.

Put them in the same frame, pointed at each other across an action sequence, and the screen should combust.

The film is produced by **Dil Raju** under **Sri Venkateswara Creations** — the Telugu powerhouse behind films like *Maharshi* and *Varisu*. The production tag itself signals the pan-India ambition: this is not a Bollywood film with a South heroine. It is a cross-industry tentpole designed to play in every language market simultaneously.

## The Bandra Schedule

The Mumbai leg is built around what the production team is calling one of the film's **major action set pieces** — a sequence that begins as a pursuit and gradually escalates into a full confrontation. The makers have chosen Bandra's streetscape specifically for its urban texture, and the sequences will feature both leads in physical action roles.

Salman, who has leaned into heavier, more grounded action in recent years — *Tiger 3* swapped the cartoonish stunts for something meaner — is reportedly performing a significant portion of the action himself. Nayanthara, who did her own fight choreography in multiple Tamil films, is expected to match him beat for beat.

After Bandra wraps, the unit moves to **Hyderabad in July** for the next major schedule.

## The Director Behind the Camera

**Vamshi Paidipally** is a National Award-winning filmmaker whose Telugu hits — *Maharshi* with Mahesh Babu, *Varisu* with Vijay — have grossed hundreds of crores while staying rooted in emotional, family-driven storytelling. His entry into Hindi cinema with Salman is a bet on the same formula: commercial spectacle with an emotional core, mounted on a scale that justifies the theatrical experience.

Production began in **April 2026**, and the makers are targeting an **Eid 2027** release — the slot Salman has owned for the better part of two decades. A title reveal is expected within the next two weeks, and insiders say the announcement video is designed to break the internet.

## For the Diaspora

For **NRI audiences** who track both Hindi and South releases, this film is the rare project that doesn't require you to pick a side. Salman's star power travels to every Indian diaspora pocket on the planet. Nayanthara's does too — just through different theatres and different WhatsApp groups. When the title drops, expect both ecosystems to light up.

The streets of Bandra are about to become a movie set. If you see barricades near Hill Road, now you know why.
